title: Template-driven forms, and why the reactive ones win as the form grows

videos.script:
Angular has more than one way to write a form, and you will meet all of them. This lesson writes the same two fields three ways, and keeps the planner's form as it is.

{{ngmodel}} First the oldest: a template-driven form, where each n g model in the template makes a control, and the class holds plain values.

{{template}} Its validators are attributes. Required and min sit on the inputs, and the template decides when a message shows.

{{catch}} Then the catch. The form only exists once the template has run, and a little after, and its values are typed as any. The bigger the form, the more that costs.

{{signals}} Then Signal Forms, new and experimental in Angular twenty-one. The model is a signal you own, and every field's state is a signal too.

{{three}} And a table to choose by. Reactive forms stay the default, and you will recognise the other two when you meet them.
